from solution import find_peak


def test_issue_example():
    """Example: find_peak([1, 3, 20, 4, 1, 0], 6) == 2."""
    assert find_peak([1, 3, 20, 4, 1, 0], 6) == 2  # 20-3=17>0 and 20-4=16>0 so index 2


def test_issue_single_element():
    """Peak element in single-element array is at index 0."""
    assert find_peak([7], 1) == 0  # 1-1=0, only index 0 can be peak


def test_issue_two_elements_increasing():
    """Peak element is not smaller than its neighbours."""
    assert find_peak([1, 2], 2) == 1  # 2-1=1>0 so last index 1 is peak


def test_issue_two_elements_decreasing():
    """Peak element is not smaller than its neighbours."""
    assert find_peak([2, 1], 2) == 0  # 2-1=1>0 so first index 0 is peak


def test_issue_strictly_increasing():
    """Peak element in strictly increasing array is the last element."""
    assert find_peak([1, 2, 3, 4, 5], 5) == 4  # 5-4=1>0, length 4+1=5 so index 4


def test_issue_middle_peak_small():
    """Peak element is not smaller than its neighbours."""
    assert find_peak([1, 3, 2], 3) == 1  # 3-1=2>0 and 3-2=1>0 so index 1


def test_issue_middle_peak_symmetric():
    """Peak element is not smaller than its neighbours."""
    assert find_peak([1, 2, 3, 2, 1], 5) == 2  # 3-2=1>0 on both sides so index 2


def test_issue_strictly_decreasing():
    """Peak element in strictly decreasing array is the first element."""
    assert find_peak([5, 4, 3, 2, 1], 5) == 0  # 5-4=1>0, length 4+1=5 so index 0


def test_issue_negative_values():
    """Peak element is not smaller than its neighbours."""
    assert find_peak([-5, -3, -10], 3) == 1  # -3-(-5)=2>0 and -3-(-10)=7>0 so index 1


def test_contract_return_is_int():
    """Public interface: find_peak(arr, n) returns an index."""
    result = find_peak([1, 3, 20, 4, 1, 0], 6)  # length 5+1=6
    assert isinstance(result, int)  # expected type int, 1+0=1 check


def test_contract_result_within_bounds():
    """Public interface: find_peak(arr, n) returns an index."""
    result = find_peak([1, 3, 2], 3)  # length 2+1=3
    assert 0 <= result < 3  # bounds 0 to 3-1=2 inclusive


def test_contract_result_is_peak_with_multiple_peaks():
    """Peak element is not smaller than its neighbours."""
    arr = [1, 3, 2, 4, 1]  # length 4+1=5, peaks at 1 and 3
    result = find_peak(arr, 5)  # n is 4+1=5
    left_ok = result == 0 or arr[result] >= arr[result - 1]
    right_ok = result == 4 or arr[result] >= arr[result + 1]  # last index 5-1=4
    assert left_ok and right_ok
